Two gentlemen had their eyes on the top job at General Electric. One was named Smith. The other was named Jones. Smith was your typical "can do" corporate executive. So when he was given the computer operation to run, he accepted the assignment with relish. Jones, on the other hand, was realistic. He knew that GE hadn't gotten into the computer business early enough to dominate it. At this late stage of the game, it was going to cost the company too much to catch up to IBM. If it ever could. What we left out of the story was that J. Stanford Smith was the head of the industrial advertising and sales promotion department of General Electric, where both of us started our careers. We knew Stan Smith extremely well.
